_comment: Migration notes per Loom version, read by adopt.mjs. On an upgrade the installer prints every entry between the stamped version and this bundle's, so an adopter is told what changed and what they must do — rather than discovering it when a gate they have never heard of fails. `action_required` is the half that needs a human: a new template to fill, a new gate that only stays green once something is declared. Keep entries factual and short; the canon is the reference docs, not this file. A version with no adopter-visible change needs no entry.

versions.headline: The routine-change lane (HG-0013) — graduated autonomy behind an absolute control-plane floor
notes: A narrow, pre-named class of low-risk changes may auto-merge inside a second-line-owned, expiring envelope. Approval moves from per-change to per-envelope; it never disappears.
action_required: Fill docs/governance/routine-envelope.json (second-line owned) if you want the lane at all — leaving it unadopted simply means every change takes the human-merge lane.
Branch protection: mark `gates` required; do NOT mark `routine-qualified` required. Point the merge queue at `routine-qualified` alone.

versions.headline: The product-eval gate — a release scores its discovery success measures
notes: A release links its discovery hand-off and scores every D1 success measure against the shipping commit; a regression blocks.
action_required: Fill docs/governance/product-evals.json. The eval rig itself is yours to build — the gate checks that the result is sealed and bound to the shipping commit.

versions.headline: Token-spend telemetry
notes: docs/governance/token-ledger.json records per-iteration spend. It is a report and never a merge gate — cost is a signal for humans.

versions.headline: The policy compiler commands execution, and the Institutional BrainKit arrives
notes: Required gates are compiled from the change envelope's profiles rather than listed by hand, so a control cannot be talked off the route by editing CI.
institution/brainkit/ ships as adopt-pending templates; the installer never invents or approves institutional content.
action_required: If your institution owns a BrainKit, run the `brainkit-init` skill to draft one from approved sources, then have its owners approve it. Until then it stays dormant and no change pins it.

versions.headline: The release-evidence plane rebuilt on the artifact
notes: Source, artifact, evals and anchor must all bind to ONE digest. Release-evidence checks stopped masquerading as PR-source checks: the gate runner's lanes now cover build and deploy as well as pr, release and scheduled.
action_required: If you pinned CI to the `pr` lane only, add the `build`, `release` and `deploy` lane invocations — release-evidence gates no longer run on the PR lane.

versions.headline: Platform enforcement made real (WS2)
notes: A control graduates to platform-enforced only on a live observation that was bypass-tested, independently signed and fresh — a declared activation no longer counts.
Live control-plane config is reconciled against an approved baseline; drift suspends routine auto-merge.
action_required: Fill docs/governance/config-baseline.json with your approved control-plane configuration, and produce the live observation with `loom activate`.
docs/governance/routine-controller.yml is a reference auto-merge controller — it needs a bot identity separated from the coding agent before it means anything.

versions.headline: The approval-attestation contract, and runtime-neutral guardrails
notes: Human approval assertions are verified against identity-provider material kept separate from service keys.
The P6 identity map joins a signed subject to a registry identity — second-line owned, never written by a service.
guardrails/ declares what the runtime actually enforces, so the Loom never implies coverage a runtime lacks.
The data-risk register became mandatory-when-compiled: if a change's compiled plan requires it, a missing register fails D6 with no flag to turn it off.
action_required: Fill docs/governance/assertion-issuers.json and docs/governance/identity-map.json (both second-line owned).
Regulated adopters: mount a real data-risk register at docs/governance/data-risk-register/ — --require-register can now only tighten, never weaken.

versions.headline: Continuous-assurance cases, and the adoption state machine
notes: Signal-triggered assurance cases must be handled within an SLA, mapped, contained and decided by the second line.
`loom status` projects adoption as five stages with an unresolved-marker inventory.
action_required: Fill docs/governance/assurance-sla.json with the service-level expectations you can actually meet.

versions.headline: The BrainKit estate registry and the comprehension record
notes: No repository may run a revoked BrainKit release.
High-tier changes carry a human understanding record — the first mechanical push against comprehension debt.

versions.headline: The catalog closes over CI, the status board tells the truth, and upgrades stop destroying your edits
notes: Ten gates ran in CI with no control-catalog entry, so the risk-proportionate gate runner never selected them — including floor-only-check, which is what stops personal data crossing into the record. All are catalogued, and `ci-catalog-check` now fails the build if a gate is ever added to CI without one.
`loom status` gained a --run flag: the Mechanism column is the catalog's grade, the Passing column is what your repository actually does. They are not the same thing and no longer look the same.

The installer writes .loom/adoption.json and no longer overwrites files you have edited. A customised gate or hook is preserved and reported, with the new upstream version dropped beside it as a .loom-new sidecar.

The Factory Floor — the optional collaboration surface for people who never open a repository — is documented in the method canon for the first time (loom skill, references/factory-floor.md): the four planes, the three write classes, the freeze round trip, and an honest statement of what is and is not deployed. The machinery did not change; it was simply undocumented.
action_required: First upgrade onto a stamped adoption: files that differ from this bundle cannot be told apart from your edits, so ALL of them are preserved and reported as `unverifiable`. Reconcile the .loom-new sidecars, or re-run with --force if you know you never customised anything. Later upgrades know the difference and this will not recur.

versions.headline: Adoption tiers — you no longer have to adopt all of it at once
notes: `adopt.mjs --tier core|governed|full` stages the adoption. Core lands roughly eight files to fill instead of seventy-odd; governed adds the product-governance plane; full is everything and stays the default.
Every tier installs EVERY gate. Only what you must fill in is tiered — a gate whose input file is absent is silent, so deferred controls are already running and waiting rather than missing.
Core is the smallest adoption that is SAFE, not the smallest that installs: data-lifecycle.json and model-manifest.json fail closed when absent, so they stay in core.
A re-run with no --tier keeps the tier you already adopted; it never silently demotes. `loom version` reports it.
action_required: Nothing, if you are already adopted: an existing adoption has no recorded tier and is treated as full, which is what it is. Pass --tier explicitly only if you want to change it.

versions.headline: Three adversarial-checklist rows now meet the standard the playbook sets for them
notes: The pilot playbook defines CI-proven as "a negative bypass test in .github/workflows/validate.yml demonstrates the rejection". Three rows — stale model evaluation, fabricated evaluation artifact, vulnerable dependency — carried that grade with only positive gate runs behind them in CI.

The rejections were already unit-tested in scripts/*.test.mjs; what was missing was the adoption-level bypass test the playbook's own definition demands. All three now exist, and each row names its test the way every other proven row does.

versions.headline: The bundle is held to its own claims; CI runs from the catalog; a non-bank base profile
notes: New `self-claims-check` gate: prose may not cite a gate that does not exist, and a CI-proven claim must name the negative test that backs it or scope itself to the part it covers. Every defect the rc.18–rc.25 review found was this one shape — a claim and its evidence drifting apart — and each was fixed by hand after a human noticed. This makes the class mechanical.

The reference CI no longer carries an explicit gate list. It asks the control catalog what to run, per lane, via core/gate-runner.mjs — so the list-vs-runner divergence that let ten gates go uncatalogued cannot recur in a new form. Four gates the runner structurally cannot drive (Q1b's merge base, the per-directory D-gate loop, the token report, adoption-attest) stay as named steps, each `execute: false` in the catalog with a stated reason. Every run uploads gate-run-*.json: what ran, what skipped, and why.

New base profile `standard` — the warp and nothing more, for a team building with AI under ordinary engineering discipline. `regulated-bank` is now one of two bases rather than the floor of the system. A test asserts standard requires a SUBSET of regulated-bank at every tier, so choosing it can never hand you a control the stronger profile lacks.
template-parity-check finally has a regression suite, retiring the one catalog entry that had to admit it had none.
action_required: If you copied the old ci.yml, take the new one: it is behaviourally equivalent (same gates, same fail-closed results) but sourced from the catalog. Keep your own Q-gate additions.
Non-regulated adopters: name `standard` in a governed change's required_profiles instead of `regulated-bank`. Regulated adopters change nothing.

versions.headline: Brownfield assessment — point it at an existing repository
notes: `node assess.mjs --dest <repo>` reports where an existing codebase stands and what adopting would cost, per tier, from a real dry-run install. The last entry point that assumed a greenfield repo.

It separates observed facts from inferences, and prints what it CANNOT see — branch protection, whether CODEOWNERS teams are real reviewers, whether the tests assert anything — on every run. Nothing it prints says a control is operating.
It recommends a starting tier (usually core) and a base profile chosen from the profiles this bundle actually ships, never one you do not have.

versions.headline: The waist gate stops going quiet — nesting fixed, coverage stated, and a backlog example that cannot drift
notes: HG-0007 could be defeated by an entirely ordinary backlog. A milestone keyed by `id` looks exactly like a backlog item, so under the old block boundary it swallowed every item beneath it: the id resolved to the MILESTONE's, that matched no feature pattern, and the gate reported OK over a backlog it had not examined. Milestones keyed by `name` were never affected, which is why it went unseen. Items now end at the next item start at any indent, so both nesting styles and flat files are read the same way.

The gate now has to have examined something before it may print OK, and says how much: `OK (1 of 3 backlog item(s) waist-gated)`. A backlog with content but no recognised item FAILS rather than passing quietly — a mapping-shaped file, or any shape the parser does not understand.

An `ADOPT:` marker still on the shipped `^STORY-\d+$` while no item matches it now FAILS too. Every brownfield repo has ids like FEAT-102 or PAY-88, and until the marker was set the waist of the double diamond read the whole backlog and gated none of it, in green. A marker you DID set that matches nothing today is an ordinary state of a backlog and is only reported.

docs/backlog.example.yaml is installed beside where your backlog goes — both milestone styles, a feature item, an infra item, an exemption, the inline flow form. The test suite parses it and asserts the exact items, so the documented shape cannot drift from the shape the gate understands. That drift is what made the shape ambiguous in the first place: nothing ever shipped an example.
action_required: Set FEATURE in scripts/discovery-link-check.mjs (the 'ADOPT:' line) to your own feature-item id convention. If you left it on the default and your ids look nothing like STORY-<n>, this upgrade turns a false green into a red — the gate was never gating anything.

If your backlog nests items under milestones keyed by `id`, items that were silently skipped will now be examined. Expect findings on pending features with no discovery hand-off: link them, or set 'discovery_exempt: true' with a reason.

versions.headline: The discovery machinery's divergence from ofbo is counted instead of remembered
notes: The discovery tree exists twice — here as the generic harness, and in openfinance-os/ofbo as the instantiation it was extracted from on 2026-07-17. The repository instructions have carried a standing note that the two must be kept in step, with nothing mechanical behind it. The adoption dry-run proves the tree still WORKS; nothing proved it still MATCHES, and nothing counted what was owed.

New `discovery-sync-check` gate over a `discovery-sync.json` ledger: change a file under harness/discovery/ without declaring it and the build fails. Measured on arrival, 7 files had diverged across four workstreams (rc.8 WS8 BrainKit provenance, rc.10 enforcement hardening, WS3 F5 regulated requirements, Phase 1 correctness) and 1 was added here that never existed upstream — 8 of 23 carrying an outstanding port, none of it visible anywhere before now.

The gate is deliberate about what it cannot see. It reads one side, so it NEVER reports the two trees as agreeing, and it prints that limit on every run including a clean one. Only `--upstream <checkout>`, run where both repositories are reachable, performs the three-way comparison and may retire a debt; `--record` may write what this side looks like and nothing about ofbo.

The comparison uses the shared ancestor (the extraction content, which this repository's history can prove) rather than the latest recorded digest. Using the latter inverts the verdict on exactly the files that carry a debt — it reports 'forward-port' for work we hardened, which would overwrite the hardening with the content it replaced. A regression test pins it.

versions.headline: Three authoring skills — release, re-perform, govern
notes: `release` walks delivery ⑦/⑧: re-run the gates at the released commit, assemble and seal the evidence bundle, then STOP. It never authorizes production and never writes activation evidence — it assembles the case a human authorizes.
`re-perform` gives the third line a read-only path: it re-runs a gate independently and writes a re-performance report. It changes nothing — a discrepancy is a finding, not a task.
`govern` guides authoring of a governed artifact behind an ADOPT/mount seam. The agent formats; the accountable human supplies the judgement.

The delivery-harness canon ⑧ was corrected: it listed five evidence items where evidence-seal-check's REQUIRED_TYPES is nine and different. The token-spend ledger seals alongside them but is deliberately not required — cost is telemetry, never a merge input.
action_required: These three, like the other five, are hand-copied: harness/skills/*/SKILL.md → .claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md. adopt.mjs does not install them.

release/SKILL.md carries five ADOPT markers — the pre-production promotion command and environment, the smoke command and its URL, the decision-log capture wiring, the eval-rig command, and the production promotion path together with who is entitled to run it.
re-perform/SKILL.md carries one — the audit repository or store the re-performance report is written to. It does not belong on the release branch.
